findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain default value, so `timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created in that process shares the same timestamp, which can be hours or days old. Any later use of `queued` (ordering, staleness checks, debugging) will be wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: Task kwargs carry a raw datetime that may not survive serialization
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, so the `queued` value passed to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` is a `datetime` object. If the Celery broker uses a JSON serializer, the enqueue call can fail; this is the inbound webhook path, so the assignment sync would break. If serialization succeeds, `queued` likely comes back as a string, and `from_dict` silently builds an object whose `queued` is not a datetime. Serialize `queued` explicitly (for example as an ISO string or timestamp) and parse it back in `from_dict`. The tests run tasks eagerly via `self.tasks()`, so they may not catch this.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` parameter on abstract `sync_status_outbound` is never used
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller passes it and status-sync cycles are not addressed anywhere in this PR. Concrete implementations do not declare the parameter either. This changes the abstract contract without effect and suggests status sync is protected against cycles when it is not.

findings.title: No test covers the inbound path that this fix targets
findings.body: The new test calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` with a hand-built `AssignmentSource`. Nothing verifies that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (assign or deassign) skips the outbound sync back to the originating integration. Nothing checks that other integrations linked to the same group still receive the sync. Nothing tests the `to_dict`/`from_dict` round trip through task serialization. The real cycle scenario therefore has no regression coverage.
